subject: Post-call: Finlytics POC - integration plan & JSON reliability safeguards
summary: Post-demo qualification and technical follow-up covering SDK/auth options, routing and model variants, structured JSON output guarantees, and retry/validation patterns for the POC.
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lowe <hannah@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-14T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps (Finlytics POC)

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) Scope & success criteria
- POC goal: reliable entity extraction + ranker for financial advisories in the product feed (target latency p50 < 350ms for per-request top-k embeddings).
- Success metric: >= 92% JSON schema pass rate on our evaluation set and reranker NDCG improvement >= 8% vs baseline.

2) Integration options we discussed
- SDK (recommended): use Redwood JS SDK for streaming + structured output helpers. We can provide a sample repo.
- Direct REST: fine for quick checks but loses helper utilities for constrained decoding.

3) Auth & networking
- We support API key, OAuth2 service accounts, and mTLS for Private deployments. For the POC, Hannah suggested SSO-backed service account keys. That will work; see checklist attached.

4) Structured output reliability
- We'll provide a JSON schema and a validation+retry pattern: initial inference -> schema validator -> if failure, run constrained decoding pass (guided decoding with schema tokens) -> if still failing, fallback to reranker-assisted extraction.
- We'll include a sample schema (attached: redwood-json-schema-proposal-v1.json) matching the entity types you enumerated.

5) Routing & model variants
- For latency-first eval use our small-quantized embedding model + reranker combo. For quality-first tests we can route to our higher-capacity model. Routing policy will be a config flag on the SDK.

6) Action items (owners)
- Finlytics: provide sample anonymized dataset + expected output schema (Hannah) — due 2026-10-20.
- Redwood: provide example SDK repo + JSON schema + validation flow (Vanessa/Aisha) — deliver by 2026-10-18.
- Redwood Eng: estimate perf requirements for constrained decoding and caching (Rafael) — TBD, aim 2026-10-22.

Attachments: finlytics-poc-credentials-checklist.pdf (checklist for service account), redwood-json-schema-proposal-v1.json

If that looks right I’ll open a HubSpot task and kick off the sample repo.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

---

Date: 2026-10-14T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps (Finlytics POC)

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful and accurate. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Dataset: we’ll provide ~5k anonymized records with the target entities plus a small set of edge cases (expected by 10/20).
- Auth: we prefer OAuth2 service account flow — need a short doc for how to exchange credentials.
- Latency: 350ms p50 is our soft target for the user-facing query; background batch reranks can be slower.

Technical question: for constrained decoding you mentioned "guided decoding with schema tokens" — can you briefly outline how that integrates with our post-processing pipeline? If you can drop a short example in the repo that’ll help our engineers.

We’re excited to get started.

— Hannah
Head of Product, Finlytics

Team — forwarding Finlytics thread. A few immediate engineering asks from the call and from Hannah’s reply:

1) Provide a short example of the constrained-decoding + validation flow for JSON outputs. Minimal example: prompt -> model -> validator -> constrained decode retry. Keep it language-agnostic (but repo will include JS).
2) Attach a lightweight validator (we can use AJV in the sample) and include a policy for retry thresholds (e.g., 2 constrained attempts then fallback).
3) Performance: Rafael, can you sketch how much extra latency constrained decoding adds on top of a baseline token-gen? Also include caching options for KV prefix caching for repeated templates.

Notes from the call:
- Embeddings + reranker: Finlytics will index product descriptions; they want an embedding dimensionality recommendation and an approach to reranker candidates (dense top-k + lightweight lexical filter).
- Auth: they want the OAuth service-account walkthrough. We can provide a short runbook and an integration checklist (I attached the checklist to the original email).

Please reply-all with ETA and any blockers so I can loop Hannah.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Quick update from eng side:

- Constrained decoding approach: two-step pattern we recommend:
  1) "Soft validator" after the first generation: run AJV (schema) against the generated JSON. If it fails, try a single constrained decoding pass usingguided token masks derived from the schema (we’ll provide a token whitelist/ordering helper) — this generally catches structural issues faster than repeated free-form retries.
  2) If constrained pass fails again, fall back to a specialized extraction model with token-level alignment (our reranker-assisted extractor) and then validate.

- Latency: constrained-decoding single pass adds roughly 50–120ms median depending on sequence length and quantization profile; a constrained pass plus reranker could push worst-case P95 above 800ms if we don’t cache KV prefixes. We’ll include caching on repeated templates and prefix caching for dialog-like repeated contexts — that should recover ~100ms in most P50 cases.

- Embeddings/ranker guidance: recommend 1536-d embeddings for your dataset size (dedup + FAISS HNSW index). Use a two-stage retrieval: dense top-100 + lexical filter -> lightweight transformer reranker (small model) for final top-10. We’ll provide a sample pipeline in the repo.

- Deliverables & ETA:
  • Example repo (JS + node): constrained decode + AJV + retry policy — ETA 2026-10-18 (Aisha/Stephanie)
  • Perf sketch (numbers for quantized model variants and expected latency hits) — ETA 2026-10-22 (Rafael)
  • OAuth runbook + checklist updated — ETA 2026-10-18 (Aisha)

I’ll attach the token-whitelist helper and a short README to the sample repo. Any concerns flag them here and I’ll triage.

-Rafael
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
